alt: A table of recorded offending and victimisation by age, class, gender and ethnicity: young, working-class and male people have the highest recorded offending, while young men, poorer areas, women and minority groups face particular kinds of victimisation. A note on repeat victimisation and how statistics are produced.
caption: Learn both sides: who offends and who is victimised.

alt: When a group appears more often in crime statistics, explanations of offending ask whether they really commit more, through lack of opportunity, status frustration, gangs, deprivation, masculinity or socialisation; explanations of the statistics ask whether they are more likely to be caught, through targeting, stereotyping, institutional racism, chivalry or the self-fulfilling prophecy.
caption: Use one explanation of each kind, then judge which matters more.

alt: Five explanations written as cause, mechanism and outcome: status frustration, lack of opportunity, relative deprivation, police targeting and the chivalry thesis. The first three explain offending; the last two explain the statistics.
caption: Cause, mechanism, crime outcome: the shape of every developed point.

alt: Merton’s strain theory: society sets goals but blocks legitimate means for some. A table shows five adaptations: conformity, innovation (such as theft), ritualism, retreatism (such as some drug addicts) and rebellion. A note adds Cloward and Ohlin’s criminal, conflict and retreatist subcultures.
caption: Innovation, using crime to reach accepted goals, is Merton’s explanation of most property crime.

alt: Labelling: primary deviance that is not labelled becomes secondary deviance once a label, possibly a master status, is applied. Below, Stanley Cohen’s deviancy amplification: media reporting of mods and rockers created folk devils, leading to tougher policing and more confrontation. A note adds Hall’s study of the mugging panic.
caption: Reactions to deviance can produce more of it.

alt: A table of five theories of crime with a key idea and limitation: functionalism does not explain middle-class crime, interactionism does not explain the first act, Marxism neglects working-class victims, feminism may treat women as one group and postmodernism offers no single cause for policy.
caption: Every theory explains some patterns and misses others.
